Each eye had an inferior symblepharon involving up to three clock hours and cicatrization of the caruncle.
Ocular examination showed bilateral moderate diffuse bulbar conjunctival hyperemia and grade 1 subtarsal papillary reaction.
response.rationale: R2 best integrates the atopic/eczematous background with bilateral chronic conjunctivitis and cicatricial ocular changes including symblepharon and caruncular scarring, indicating atopic keratoconjunctivitis as the specific cause of chronic cicatricial conjunctivitis. R1 only restates the clinical category, while R3, R4, and R5 each capture only part of the picture.

rejected.why: Tear-film instability and blurred vision are secondary features; dry eye syndrome does not explain symblepharon or conjunctival cicatrization.
It restates the already given umbrella diagnosis and lacks specificity for the atopic etiologic cause.
Explains the skin rash but not the ocular cicatricial conjunctival pathology.
Meibomian gland and eyelash findings are contributory but cannot explain symblepharon or caruncular scarring.
